scenario: WIBTA for selling what I receive in my dad's will? | Obligatory "I'm on mobile, so sorry for mistakes." I (22M) have a very large family. Both of my parents have 3 kids from past relationships, and I'm the only child they have together. My dad (71) never divorced his previous wife, but has been with my mom (61) for the past 25 years. My dad is a severe alcoholic and has a bunch of other health problems. So the talk of his will has come up a few times. He owns the house we currently live in, his (separated) wife's house, and a bar that has 2 apartments above it. As of now, his wife's house would remain her's or if she passes, go to their 3 children. The house we live in now, would be split amongst the 4 of us. I personally want nothing to do with the bar due it being a cause for my parent's alcoholism. My mom says I should just give it all to her if that's the case. I would ask her to at least buy out my half, but she has been mentally abusive to me for most of my life, and constantly sabotaged anything I've done to try and better my own life. I've recently thought about just selling my quarter of the house to my siblings, and the entire bar to them or anyone else who wants it. WIBTA if I decided to leave my mom out of anything I get from my dad's will?

Excluding her entirely might feel justified, but it could also be a missed opportunity for reconciliation or even a witness to her of God’s grace. 2. **Stewardship of Inheritance (Proverbs 13:22, Luke 16:10-12)** - Inheritance is a gift from God, not just a human right. Selling the bar to others (not her) isn’t wrong if it’s for a good purpose (e.g., financial freedom, avoiding temptation, or helping siblings). 4. **The Bar as a Symbol of Struggle (1 Corinthians 6:12, 10:23)** - You mentioned the bar is tied to your parents’ alcoholism. If you sell the bar and house to others (not her), that’s not wrong—**but it should be done with a heart of freedom, not vengeance**. Would you consider a middle path where you still bless your siblings (who may not have the same emotional baggage) while ensuring your mom doesn’t gain anything from your portion?
